status: Written on 2026-10-20 before any 2048-hour forecast was run. The 336-hour results were already seen, so this is a planned follow-up, not an untouched confirmation.
question: Do the 336-hour conclusions hold when Chronos-Bolt gets up to its standard 2048-hour history, in particular the cases where the validation-selected baseline turns a clear Chronos win into an unclear result?
change: History length 336 -> up to 2048 hours. Model commit, cases, test origins, baselines, blend weights, 0.5 quantile and bootstrap settings are unchanged.
context_policy: Up to 2048 hours ending at the origin; all available history when the series starts later (Q1); missing hours passed as NaN, which Chronos-Bolt masks.
clear_result: Paired circular-block bootstrap from src/chronos_uncertainty.py (5,000 resamples, 168- and 336-hour blocks, same seeds). Clear means both 95% intervals favour the same method; otherwise unclear; household windows with too few blocks are limited.
claim_change: Chronos clearly beats weekly naive but not the validation-selected baseline, or the reverse.
meaningful_improvement: A clear Chronos win with an MAE gain of at least 5% against the comparator. 2% and 10% are reported as sensitivity checks.
sanity_check: Q4 Tetouan at 168 hours should be close to the earlier 2048-hour run on the same test window: MAE about 696, 756 and 544 for zones 1 to 3.
reporting: Report both history lengths side by side and keep the 336-hour results. Report Q1 separately because its history is shorter than 2048 hours. Q4 repeats the original test period and is not new evidence. No multiple-comparison correction; exploratory.
